sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 02.06.2023.
2.

The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 02.06.2023 at about 11.15 p.m., petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-03-JR-5371 slowly, cautiously and observing all traffic rules, at that time a Car bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AJ-8400 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, applied sudden break and stopped the Car without any indications or indicators.
Suddenly the passenger opened the right side door.
Due to sudden opening of the door, door dashed against to the motorcycle and due to the tremendous impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained multiple injuries all over the body.

Immediately, he was shifted to Uvin Care Hospital, Bangalore, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Chinmaya Mission Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance, food,
transport and other charges.

The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 19 years, the petitioner was a B.E. Student studying at Dayananda Sagar college of Engineering and also working as a part-time computer operator and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.2 remained absent.
Hence, placed exparte.
The respondent No.1 filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition.

Further,
this respondent admits the issuance of policy to the alleged offending vehicle and policy was inforce Prajwal Sai Manikanta.S vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3870683/
2 as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 134(c) and 158(6) of M. V. Act.
It is further submitted that, the driver of offending Car was not holding valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident.
Further, this respondent denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he is the victim of the motor vehicle accident caused by the driver of the Car bearing Reg.
No. KA-03-AJ-8400 at about 11.15 p.m., on channel road, 2nd Main, Saraswathipuram, Halasuru,
Bengaluru and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that, he is not liable to pay compensation as pleaded in the written statement?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

4. What order or Award?
5.

In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.13 and examined MRT at Chinmaya Mission Hospital as P.W.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.16 and also examined Dr. S. U. Shiva Prakash as P.W.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.19 and also examined Dr. Sreedhara K. C as PW.4 and got marked documents at Ex.P.20 to Ex.P.22 and closed their side.
On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.

sentences.text: The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 13.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the Sketch, Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report,
Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is the charge-sheet, Ex.P.8 is the Discharge Summary, Ex.P.9 is the Medical Bills, Ex.P.10 is the Prescription, Ex.P.11 is the Lab Report, Ex.P.12 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card and Ex.P.13 is the Notarized copy of Driving License.

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that 02.06.2023 at about 11.15 p.m., petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-03-JR-5371 slowly, cautiously and observing all traffic rules, at that time a Car bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AJ-8400 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, applied sudden break and stopped the Car without any indications or indicators.
Suddenly the passenger opened the right side door.
Due to sudden opening of the door, door dashed against to the motorcycle and due to the tremendous impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained multiple injuries all over the body.

Immediately, he was shifted to Uvin Care Hospital,
Bangalore, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Chinmaya Mission Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient. Accordingly, the Halasur Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.106/2023.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
11.
The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Halasur Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P.2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 106/2023.

The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P.1.
12.

During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P1 to 7 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the driver of offending Car.

The Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.4 (Spot panchanama and Sketch), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.7, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the offending private Bus punishable U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC.
The Ex.P.5 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.
13. On the other hand, contesting respondent has not denied the accident in question.
Except suggestions and denial insurance company has not produced any documents to show that, accident is caused due to the negligence of petitioner also.

14. In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA- 03-AJ-8400.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Uvin Care Hospital, wherein first-aid treatment was given and then shifted to Chinmaya Mission Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
16. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

In the petition as well as in his evidence PW.1 deposed that,
immediately after the accident he was shifted to Chinmay Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 03.06.2023 to 06.06.2023 i.e., for 03 days.
The petitioner has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.8 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the said hospitals for 03 days.

He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, which reveals that, petitioner has sustained HEAD INJURY AND PARIETO - TEMPORAL EXTRADURAL HEMORRHAGE WITH FRACTURE OF TEMPORAL PARIETAL BONE RIGHT SIDE and the doctor has opined that the injury is grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
17. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of his plea, he has produced the 23 medical bills which is marked at Ex.P.9 to the tune of Rs.70,072/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.70,072/- towards medical expenses.
18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.8 Discharge summary issued by Specialist Hospital, Bangalore, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 03.06.2023 to 06.06.2023 i.e., for 03 days.
Hence, at least 02 month is required to recover from the accidental injuries.
It is further contended that, the injured petitioner was a student and also working as computer operator, in support of his income he has not produced any single document.

So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,000/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench.

Hence, 02 month is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/- under this head.

20. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner/injured has to be determined.
Ex.P.12 is the Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his DOB is mentioned as 06.12.2004 and accident took place in the year 2023.
Accordingly, I assess his age as 19 years at the time of this accident.
As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '18'.

Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Chinmany Mission Hospital, Bangalore as inpatient from 03.06.2023 to 06.06.2023 i.e., for 03 days.

Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/-
under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges.
22. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 19 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
It shows that he found difficulty in doing day to day works.
He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.30,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,23,272/- under various heads.
23. LIABILITY:
As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AJ-8400.

The respondent No.1 issued the policy to the offending vehicle valid from 02.02.2023 to 01.02.2024 and accident occurred on 02.06.2023,
thus the policy was in-force as on the date of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.
24. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.9,23,272/- with interest @ 6%

The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

7 above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 50% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon.
Remaining 50% of compensation amount of  petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
